Use legacy FEniCS (dolfin, not dolfinx) to solve a 2D plane-stress linear elasticity problem on a parallelogram domain.
Define the parallelogram with vertices (0,0), (1,0), (1.2,0.3), (0.2,0.3) and mesh it with exactly 72 triangular elements, ensuring the point (1.1, 0.15) is a mesh vertex so it can serve as a PointSource location.
Use a vector-valued continuous Lagrange (P1) element for the displacement field on the 2D domain with unit thickness.
Apply the reduced plane-stress constitutive law with Young's modulus E = 70e9 Pa and Poisson ratio nu = 0.33.
Clamp (fix all displacement components) on the left inclined edge running from vertex (0,0) to vertex (0.2, 0.3).
Apply a body force (gravity) equal to rho * g = 2700 * 9.81 = 26487 N/m^3 acting in the negative y-direction.
Apply a horizontal point load of -5000 N in the x-direction at the mesh vertex (1.1, 0.15) using a dolfin PointSource on the x-component of the displacement variational form.
Assemble the global stiffness matrix and force vector from the plane-stress bilinear form and load linear form, then solve the resulting linear system using a direct solver (LU).
After solving, compute the in-plane Cauchy stress tensor from the displacement gradient using the plane-stress constitutive relation.
Compute the von Mises equivalent stress at each integration point from the in-plane stress components (sigma_xx, sigma_yy, sigma_xy).
Output (print or save via XDMF/CSV) the displacement field and the von Mises stress distribution over the 72-element parallelogram mesh.
